Subject: Relevance slices, SDK auth flow & top_k evaluation — next steps

Thanks again for the demo earlier — quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope the pilot (short bullets so it's actionable).

Goal: validate a hybrid retrieval + rerank pipeline for your internal KB and product docs, measure relevance uplift, and optimize production defaults (latency/cost trade-offs).

Highlights / asks from our call:
- Data slices: you said there are 3 primary retrieval slices (API docs, support transcripts, release notes). Please confirm approximate sizes and a POI for each.
- Eval set: we need your ~1k labeled queries (gold labels) + 5k unlabeled queries to run A/B and stability tests.
- Auth & infra: confirm whether you want OIDC (Okta) or service-account API keys for Redwood SDK in staging.
- Routing: confirm routing policy preference — region-first vs. cost-first; we recommend region-first for initial pilot.
- Reranker plan: high-level suggestion we gave — retrieve 100 candidates, rerank top 20, serve top_k to UI (default top_k=5). We should tune these numbers per slice.
- Metrics & stop criteria: baseline NDCG@5 / MRR; measure latency p95 and cost per 1k queries; aim for <200ms p95 on user paths or agree on fallback.

Attachments: MVP-eval-templates.xlsx (simple spreadsheet with slice definitions and label format).
Drive: mutual action plan + timelines: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-example-mutual-action-plan

Next steps (proposed):
1) You share a sample of labeled queries and schema for slices (EOD Tue 23 Jun).
2) Confirm auth approach (OIDC vs API keys) and whether Redwood can get a staging Okta client (Connor will follow up on token exchange flow).
3) Technical workshop to pair on SDK auth + routing + structured output (30–45m) — propose Wed 23 Jun 10:00 PT.
4) We run a 2-week pilot: ingestion + retrieval baseline -> rerank experiments -> report.

Ping Marcus and Connor on engineering-level asks below; I'll coordinate schedule and HubSpot updates.

Thanks — H.

--

Appreciate it — Ethan

Subject: Re: Relevance slices, SDK auth flow & top_k evaluation — next steps

Hi Ethan / Meera — Connor from Solutions Engineering here. Short technical notes ahead of Wed's workshop and a tiny SDK snippet you can try in staging.

Auth / token exchange:
- Redwood supports OIDC/OAuth flows. For Okta we recommend setting up a confidential client and an authorization server that issues short-lived access tokens.
- We offer a token-introspection endpoint and optional token-exchange layer (we can host a lightweight exchange if you prefer not to expose client secrets).
- If you want mutual TLS for service-to-service, we also support that via our Private deployment (let us know).

Routing + failover:
- Example routing policy JSON (managed in Console): region_priority -> preferred_region: us-west-2, fallback_regions: [us-east-1]; cost_tier thresholds to allow cheaper model fallback for low-priority routes.

Rerank sizing guidance (initial pilot):
- Retrieval: 100 candidates (recall-focused).
- Reranker input: score top 30 candidates; rerank and return top_k to client. Start with top_k=5 for UI, tune by slice.
- Latency: reranking 30 items with our quantized models typically adds ~40–120ms depending on model and batch size; expect ~120–350ms p95 total with retrieval + rerank for several enterprise setups. We'll instrument p50/p95 in Console.

Batching & KV cache:
- For interactive UI, use continual batching with max wait 10–20ms and an autoscaling policy.
- KV cache helps when users navigate sequentially (prefix reuse); not terribly helpful for one-off queries.

Evaluation rubric (quick):
- Primary: NDCG@5, MRR, Recall@100 (pre-rerank).
- Secondary: pairwise agreement (fraction of pairwise prefs preserved), SERP diversity per slice.
- Stability checks: run weekly holdout evaluation and regression alerts (we'll set up an eval job).

SDK snippet (Python) — quick auth + rerank call (staging):

from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(issuer_url="https://okta.myorg.com", client_id="<id>", client_secret="<secret>")

# retrieval -> rerank flow (pseudo):
recall = client.retrieval.search(index_id="kb_api_docs", query="How do I create a webhook?", top_k=100)
candidates = [r['doc_id'] for r in recall['results']]
rerank_resp = client.ranker.rerank(model="redwood-rerank-v1", inputs=candidates, query="How do I create a webhook?", top_k=5)
print(rerank_resp['results'])

I'll attach a short zip with expanded snippets and a sample routing config (redwood-sdk-snippets.zip). We'll walk through exchanging an Okta token for a Redwood session token in the workshop.

Connor O'Brien
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.ai

- Batching: how does batching interact with strict p95 targets for interactive flows? Can we configure a max-batch-delay=10ms?
- Tool-calling: we want the streaming structured output example that includes a small tool-call to create a ticket (json schema + sample). Ethan and I will review before Wed.

Confirming Wed 23 Jun 10:00 PT for the hands-on session. We'll invite our infra engineer (token owner) to join.

Best,
Meera
